status_summary: The administration asked Congress to end MEP funding in both its FY 2026 and FY 2027 budgets, matching the Mandate's recommendation, but Congress funded MEP at $175.0 million in P.L. 119-74 (2026-01-23), and CRS reports the FY 2027 request again includes no MEP funding. Trade press reports that the administration stopped funding for centers in ten states on 2025-04-01 and reversed the decision within weeks, and that NIST said on 2025-10-10 that it had decided to end the federal program. Contract renewals ran late in 2026: 13 state centers due for renewal by 2026-07-01 were waiting, and 12 had received awards by 2026-07-06, per IndustryWeek. NIST posted a notice of funding on 2026-07-22 to select center operators in 14 states and territories for five-year awards with a 50 percent non-federal cost share, while stating that only the first year is committed and that the FY2027 President's Budget would eliminate federal MEP funding. Senators Cantwell and Peters asked GAO on 2026-06-25 to examine whether Commerce's handling of MEP violated appropriations law. No legislation to zero out or privatize MEP has been enacted.

timeline.event: The administration stops funding for MEP centers with contracts up for renewal in ten states (about $13 million); the decision was reversed in mid-April, with funding continuing through the end of that fiscal year, according to trade press citing Rep. Sharice Davids.

IndustryWeek reports (in an article dated 2025-11-19) that NIST's acting director wrote on this date that NIST decided to end the federal MEP program because it is not consistent with Commerce Secretary Lutnick's priorities, and that a NIST spokesperson tied this to the FY2026 request, which zeroed out MEP; Congress had appropriated FY2026 MEP funding in September 2025.
P.L. 119-74 funds MEP at $175.0 million for FY2026, unchanged from FY2025; the Administration had requested no MEP funding.

IndustryWeek reports the FY2027 budget calls for eliminating MEP ($175 million, part of $993 million in proposed NIST cuts) and that nine state MEPs with an April 1 contract deadline had not received finalized contracts.
CRS reports the FY2027 request includes no funding for MEP, against $175.0 million enacted for FY2026.

Senators Cantwell and Peters ask GAO to examine NIST's and Commerce's handling of MEP since 2025-01-20, including whether it violated appropriations law. The letter states (as the senators' account) that NIST began withholding and delaying MEP center funds on 2025-04-01, that centers were pressed to accept new agreement terms, that Commerce's 2026-03-20 reply to a December 2025 letter from 28 senators did not give the information requested, and that Commerce cited Inspector General reviews as its justification.
timeline.source: Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation (minority)

timeline.event: IndustryWeek reports 13 state MEPs awaiting federal renewals due by July 1 (twelve had received awards by July 6), that Senators Cantwell and Peters asked GAO on June 25 to examine whether Commerce circumvented congressional directives on MEP, and that Alaska and California no longer have MEPs.

NIST posts the MEP Center State Competition (FY2026 Round 2, opportunity 2026-NIST-MEP-02) to select operators for centers in 14 locations (Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, California, Georgia, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Missouri, Montana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Utah, Vermont and Puerto Rico), with about $46.5 million in first-year federal funding (about $232 million over five years by the NOFO's table), a 50 percent non-federal cost share, applications due 2026-08-21 and an expected start of 2026-10-01. The NOFO says only Year 1 is committed, later years depend on annual appropriations, and the FY2027 President's Budget would eliminate federal funding for NIST MEP; it describes no transition to self-sufficiency.

title: Zero out and privatize NIST's Hollings Manufacturing Extension Partnership
uncertainties: Pass 5: the NIST competition page and the NOFO were read, and the senators' 2026-06-25 letter to GAO was read (it states the senators' account, not findings). The 2025-04-01 funding stop is supported by that letter as the senators' account; the 2025-10-10 NIST statement, the April 2025 reversal and the July 2026 contract renewals still rest on trade press, and the NIST memo itself was not read. Sources differ on whether the April 2025 funding stop was fully reversed (one reports a reversal, another says ten agreements were allowed to lapse); the timeline follows the reversal report. The FY2026 enacted level comes from CRS ($175.0 million, versus the Mandate's roughly $150 million figure). House and Senate committee action on MEP for FY2027 was not found.
